name: Target training
purpose: So your bird learns to touch the tip of a stick for a reward, a simple tool that can guide them almost anywhere.
done_when: your bird will travel to wherever the stick points. If the stick itself is scary, start by rewarding calm with it in view, or change its look with a colorful bead on the end.
safety_notes: Keep sessions short.
Stop at the first sign of stress.
Never withhold food to make a bird hungrier for training.

milestones.done_line: stayed calm with the target stick

milestones.title: Taps the stick tip when it's held close (with the top of the beak or tongue, not a bite).
milestones.ask: tap the tip of the stick

milestones.title: Takes a step or two to reach the stick.

name: Step up
purpose: So your bird steps onto your hand calmly and by choice, foot first, without biting.
done_when: your bird steps up on cue from most places. If your bird lowers its head, opens its beak, or leans away, it's saying no, so pause and make the next ask smaller.
safety_notes: Keep sessions short.
Stop at the first sign of stress.
Never withhold food to make a bird hungrier for training.

name: Wing touch
purpose: So your bird is comfortable having wings touched and gently extended, for vet exams and health checks. The bird gives consent at every step.
done_when: your bird leans in for wing touches and allows a short, gentle extension. Any resistance means going back a step. This one should never be rushed, and it should stay brief, since prolonged body touch can trigger hormonal behavior.
safety_notes: Keep sessions short.
Stop at the first sign of stress.
Never withhold food to make a bird hungrier for training.

name: Diet conversion
purpose: So your bird moves gradually from a seed-heavy diet to pellets, chop, and fresh foods without losing weight.
done_when: the new diet is most of what your bird eats and their weight has held steady the whole way.
safety_notes: Keep sessions short.
Stop at the first sign of stress.
Never withhold food to make a bird hungrier for training.
safeguards: Daily weigh-ins are part of every step, and the journey shows the weight trend right on its page.
The old food is never removed until the bird is reliably eating the new one.
If weight drops, the journey pauses with a clear message to call your avian vet. For app premium members, this uses the bird's own baseline alerts.
The template suggests a vet check before starting, especially for older birds or birds on an all-seed diet.
tips: Offer the new food first thing in the morning, with the usual food alongside.
Eat it in front of them. Parrots are flock eaters and often try what they see you eat.
Change one thing at a time, and go slower than feels necessary. Some birds take months, and that's normal.
Try different forms: chopped, warmed, crumbled over a favorite food, or tucked into a foraging toy.
Watch droppings and appetite as well as weight. If your bird stops eating, put the usual food back and call your vet.
Weigh in grams at the same time every day. A few grams matter on a bird.
Some birds will refuse new food so firmly that they stop eating. If your bird isn't eating, go back to the usual food today and call your vet.
Take uneaten fresh food out after a few hours so it doesn't spoil.
Notice how your bird likes food already: warm or cool, soft or crunchy, chopped fine or in chunks. Offer the new food the same way.
If your bird picks out the old food, crumble it finely over the new food and use a little less each day.
How much to feed varies from bird to bird, even within a species. Your vet can tell you what's right for yours.

name: Wave
purpose: So your bird lifts a foot and waves on cue. It builds on step up, since the wave starts as the beginning of a step up.
done_when: your bird waves to a hand signal. Stick with one foot, and only reward that foot.
safety_notes: Keep sessions short.
Stop at the first sign of stress.
Never withhold food to make a bird hungrier for training.

milestones.ask: lift it to the same height most times
milestones.done_line: lifted it the same way each time

milestones.ask: wave to your hand signal

milestones.title: Waves on cue from a little distance.
milestones.ask: wave on cue from a distance

name: Spin
purpose: So your bird turns a full circle on the perch. Pick one direction and stay with it until the spin is solid.
done_when: a finger flick gets a full spin.
safety_notes: Keep sessions short.
Stop at the first sign of stress.
Never withhold food to make a bird hungrier for training.

name: Recall
purpose: So your bird comes to you when you say their name, which is the most important safety skill if they ever get out.
done_when: your bird comes the first time you call, from anywhere in the room. Use the bird's name alone as the cue, and for very clingy birds, reward them back on the perch as well as on your hand.
safety_notes: Keep sessions short.
Stop at the first sign of stress.
Never withhold food to make a bird hungrier for training.

milestones.ask: walk across the perch to your hand
